preamble: BG has the same meaning throughout

clue.text: Golden garment on back of film needs training to relieve stress

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
TOG is a garment, as in togs for clothes

indicators.note: back of here means the word for film is read backwards

parts.note: cine is a short word for film, as in cine camera

explanation.surface: A gilded costume worn on the reverse of a film needs some coaching to ease tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' is the reversal signal, though it reads like the rear of a reel of film; 'on' and 'needs' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Autogenic training is a recognised self-relaxation technique used to relieve stress and anxiety.

clue.text: Old storyteller makes one sit up

parts.note: A means one, the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word for sit is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: An ancient teller of tales makes somebody sit upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the reversal signal, which suits a down entry read from the bottom; 'makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek fabulist of the sixth century BC is the most famous ancient teller of fables.

clue.text: Work's inside and out which is good for plant

indicators.note: one word for work goes inside while another goes on the outside around it

parts.note: toil is hard work
ops (opera, works) is a plural of op, a work

explanation.surface: A job done both indoors and outdoors is beneficial for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' supplies two different synonyms, one inside the other, which 'inside and out' tells you to nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The fertile upper layer of soil is where plants grow and draw their nourishment.

clue.text: BG is upbeat

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word for beat reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to flog is to beat

explanation.surface: A ball game is described as cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: BG stands for ball game throughout, as the preamble hints. 'upbeat' splits into 'up' (the turnaround) and 'beat' (FLOG).
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a game played with a small ball struck into holes.

clue.text: Two thirds of one or more anaesthetised

indicators.note: keeping two of the three syllable-pairs means dropping the last two letters of six

parts.note: grammatical number is singular (one) or plural (more)

explanation.surface: Two thirds of a group of people have been given a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER loses its final third, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anaesthetised leaves a body part without feeling, deadened to sensation.

clue.text: Pinch roses out with blue pencil?

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the two words being rearranged

explanation.surface: Snip off the roses with a blue pencil in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue pencil is an editor's tool for cutting text, so it stands for the act of suppressing material.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil is to cut objectionable material, which is what official suppression of text does.

clue.text: 11 for BG good in stone

indicators.note: in places the letter for good inside the gemstone

parts.note: a ruby is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Football as a ball game, with something good set in a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is the answer to 11 across, FOOTBALL; rugby is one football code.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby football is a kind of football, the ball game played with an oval ball.

clue.text: BG's tale unfolded during rise of transgressor

indicators.note: during puts the rearranged tale within the reversed word
in a down entry rise of means the word for transgressor reads upwards

parts.note: a sinner is a transgressor

indicators.note: unfolded signals the letters of tale being opened out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A story about a ball game emerges as a wrongdoer rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns SINNER into RENNIS; EALT (the letters of 'tale' reworked) goes inside after R. The 's of BG's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis is the original indoor racket and ball game played in walled courts.

clue.text: They are played by less than virtuous Scots sailors

indicators.note: less than full means the Scots word loses its last letter

parts.note: guid is Scots for good
tars are sailors

explanation.surface: Scottish seamen who are not entirely good get played.
explanation.walkthrough: GUID less D gives GUI, then TARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Guitars are stringed instruments that people play.

clue.text: Solvers' spelling defective? Let people accept thus

parts.note: ye is the old plural you, addressing the solvers
SP is the teacher's margin note for faulty spelling
to lease is to let property to people

explanation.surface: Solvers whose spelling is poor should let others agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sp' in a margin marks a spelling mistake, so 'spelling defective' gives SP.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the phrase is how one accepts an offer gladly, so it means accepting in that way.

clue.text: Flexible chaps have time to sign extra questions

parts.note: supple means flexible
chaps are men
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Bendy fellows have time to sign on for more questions.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the follow-up questions MPs ask a minister in the UK Parliament after a first answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament, further questions following a main question are known by this name.

clue.text: BG made of water

explanation.surface: A ball game consisting of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool is a cue game; a pool is also a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Pool is a billiard-table ball game, and a pool is a small body of still water.

clue.text: BG needs it to dance at dance

parts.note: to foot it is to dance
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A ball game needs you to dance at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Football is a ball game played by kicking.

clue.text: Paper money expert in soldiers' company tried it out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are being worked into a new order

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A financial specialist among a company of soldiers has had a go.
explanation.walkthrough: A city editor runs the financial pages of a British newspaper, 'the City' being London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: On a newspaper, the editor of the financial pages handles money matters.

clue.text: Neck problem: steer off from people in BG

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck

indicators.note: off signals the letters of steer being disordered

explanation.surface: A stiff neck: steer away from the players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal, though it reads as steering away; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers are the players of cricket, the bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Poet's got sick individual inside BG

indicators.note: inside places the sick individual within the poet's word

parts.note: a bard is a poet, with S for the possessive
ill means sick
I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A poet has caught a sick person inside a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue game played with balls on a cloth table.

clue.text: BG of no importance

explanation.surface: A ball game that does not matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bagatelle is a table game of balls and pins; a bagatelle is also a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a pin-and-ball table game, and also a trifling matter of no significance.

clue.text: Girl in Marylebone Station

indicators.note: in tells us the name is contained within these words

explanation.surface: A girl waits at a London railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: Marylebone is a London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesta is a girl's name, a Welsh form of Agnes.

clue.text: Fellow restraining good one with irregular blows

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the good one goes inside

parts.note: a guy is a fellow
ST, saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A man holds back a virtuous person while dealing random punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows' looks like punches but is wind blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather comes in sudden irregular bursts of wind.

clue.text: In Peterborough there's no right for BG

indicators.note: in places the word no within the old name for the district

parts.note: the Soke of Peterborough was a historic administrative area of England

explanation.surface: In Peterborough there is no entitlement to a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue game played with fifteen reds and six colours on a table.

clue.text: Say what's wrong and Spooner's town bursts into tears

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: a city is a town
to burst into tears is to cry, so cries

explanation.surface: Point out faults, and a man named Spooner's home town starts weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the C and CR of 'city cries' gives 'critty size', which sounds out the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise is to find fault, pointing out what is wrong.

clue.text: Poise established about the house, God willing?

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the house
established suggests the letters of poise being set up in a new order

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Composure is settled around the home, with any luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'established' is an unusual anagram signal, meaning the letters of the first word are set up afresh; the question mark marks the definition as a phrase in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the phrase expresses hope that something will happen, like God willing.

clue.text: Ambiguous model gets stuck holding ring

parts.note: the Model T was the famous Ford car

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the ring goes within

parts.note: wedged means stuck fast
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model is jammed in while clutching a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-edged remark cuts both ways, so it is ambiguous.

clue.text: BG version of 10, also with water

indicators.note: version of means the letters of 10 are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 10 across is POOL

explanation.surface: A rearranged form of a game that is also played in water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'also with water' adds that water polo exists too, an extra hint to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a ball game played on horseback with mallets.

clue.text: Start being filmed?

explanation.surface: Begin to be filmed.
explanation.walkthrough: An actor on set is being filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means the start of something; on set describes being in front of the camera.

clue.text: Suffering from depression maybe acquired at BG

explanation.surface: Gloomy, perhaps, after a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, a Blue is awarded for representing the university at a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means depressed; a Blue is earned by playing for Oxford or Cambridge at sport.

clue.text: Edible rubbish

explanation.surface: Garbage you can eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spam is a tinned meat; spam is also junk email.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a brand of tinned luncheon meat, and the word means unwanted junk messages.

clue.text: Appreciate favourable reception very quickly

parts.note: to like is to appreciate
the clappers are an applauding audience giving a warm reception

explanation.surface: Enjoy a warm welcome from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like the clappers' is British slang for very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means at great speed, as fast as possible.

clue.text: The Queen right or wrong?

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Is the monarch correct or mistaken?
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a wrong, a mistake.

clue.text: Craft of American snake — leave it outside

indicators.note: outside means the editing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to leave text as it was
a boa is a snake

explanation.surface: A vessel belonging to a US serpent, told to leave things alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave it' is stet, the Latin for 'let it stand' used by proofreaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamboat is a vessel, a craft driven by steam.
